reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 the KEY IS data-name-1 of an indexed READ must name the prime RECORD KEY or an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY item of file-name-1 (possibly qualified, never subscripted or reference-modified), or the item at the identical character positions in another record description entry of that file, which IX.2.7.4 GR3 and IX.2.5.4 GR4 make implicit keys; any other item (a non-key field, another file's key, a working-storage item, a REDEFINES or prefix of the key, the record itself) must be refused.

edition.Cite chooses the shape refusal's wording (§1985:IX.4.5.3 SR3 at 85); text only

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the key identity (KeyIndexOfKeyItem) is one code at every edition and rk_pos printed the same records at 85 and 2023; only the subscript admission differs, at 2002.

reader.notes: KeyIndexOfKeyItem answers the declared key by identity, then the implicit key of another record description at the same offset and width with the same class, category and usage (kb/Work PB5794, PB5877); every refusal probed was refused. The COBOL0864 refusal text cites §2023:14.9.30.3 SR11 even at --std 85 (the shape refusal alone is edition-cited), a wording matter only. rk_numeric.cob's item was not at a key position, so the numeric-twin case rests on the witness pb5794.

refuter.evidence: SR2 admits only a data item specified as a record key associated with file-name-1; IX.2.7.4 GR3 and IX.2.5.4 GR4 say the identical CHARACTER POSITIONS are implicitly referenced as keys for the other record descriptions and say nothing of the class, category or usage of an item there. The compiler (RecordLayout.KeyIndexOfKeyItem with SameClassCategoryUsage) admits a twin in another record only when its class, category and usage equal the key's, a condition no 1985 text states (it is the 2023 START generic-key condition). Probes at --std 85 (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-245/src/): rk_grouptwin.cob (group IX-G, 4 characters at X(4) IX-KEY's positions in a second record) ACCEPTED and read FS=00 0002DATA2; rk_numtwin.cob (PIC 9(4) twin) COBOL0864; rk_aetwin.cob (PIC XX/X twin, alphanumeric edited) COBOL0864; rk_grouptwin_prefix.cob (2-character prefix) COBOL0864; rk_split.cob (2023 SOURCE key form) COBOL0900. Reading 1 (strict: only the item named in a RECORD KEY or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is specified as a record key): rk_grouptwin and the reader's IMPLICIT and IMPLALT probes should be refused, so the compiler under-rejects. Reading 2 (positional: any item at the identical positions is a key): the numeric and alphanumeric-edited twins should be accepted, so the compiler rejects legal source. Only a third reading, that an implicit key item must itself qualify under §1985:IX.2.7.3 SR2 (category alphanumeric), matches the compiler; the text does not state it and the reader's verdict rests on it without saying so. cite: OK  §1985:IX.4.5.3 SR2  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2; OK  §1985:IX.2.7.4 GR3  (2.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3; OK  §1985:IX.2.5.4 GR4  (2.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4; OK  §1985:IX.2.7.3 SR2  (2.7.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2.

refuter.corrected: CONFORMS only under the unstated reading that an implicit key item must itself qualify as a key under §1985:IX.2.7.3 SR2; under either plain reading (strict or positional) one arm is wrong. The reading needs an adjudication note.

adjudication.reason: The doubt is rejected: an item at the record key's character positions in another record description is an implicit key (§1985:IX.2.7.4 GR3) when a key could be it (alphanumeric, §1985:IX.2.7.3 SR2); a group twin is, numeric, edited and prefix twins are not. The reading is kb/Work PB354's and PB5794's.
